items.headline: Mexico vs South Africa opens 2026 World Cup
items.body: <cite index="1-15">Mexico hosts South Africa in the opening match at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City on June 11</cite>. <cite index="2-30">The tournament runs from June 11 to July 19, 2026</cite>, marking the first World Cup to expand to 48 teams across three host nations.

items.headline: 48-team format brings historic expansion
items.body: <cite index="2-32">The tournament will be the first FIFA World Cup to be hosted by three nations and the first to include 48 teams, an expansion from 32 previously</cite>. <cite index="1-19,1-20">32 teams will advance to the knockout round following the group stage; the top two teams from each group will move on along with the eight best third-place teams</cite>.

items.headline: USA begins Group D campaign Friday
items.body: <cite index="1-2">The United States will begin its tournament June 12 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California against Paraguay</cite>. <cite index="1-8">The Americans will then play Australia before finishing the group stage against Türkiye</cite>.

items.headline: Canada faces Bosnia in Toronto
items.body: <cite index="1-9">Canada is in Group B and will open against Bosnia and Herzegovina on June 12 at BMO Field in Toronto</cite>. <cite index="11-23">Canada will compete alongside Switzerland, Qatar, and Bosnia and Herzegovina</cite>.

items.headline: Mexico anchors Group A as regional powerhouse
items.body: <cite index="11-3,11-4">Mexico is in Group A alongside South Africa, Korea Republic, and Czechia. As a host nation, Mexico opens the tournament in Mexico City and plays group-stage matches in Guadalajara and Monterrey</cite>.

items.headline: Netherlands loses Timber to groin injury
items.body: <cite index="20-1">Defender Jurriën Timber departed the team's camp due to a lingering groin injury, saying he was not recovered enough to participate in the World Cup in a medically responsible manner</cite>. <cite index="21-6">Despite appearing in the Champions League final, he hasn't shown enough progress, leading the Dutch team to replace him with Lutsharel Geertruida</cite>.

items.headline: Germany ruled out 18-year-old Karl
items.body: <cite index="21-17,21-18">Germany will be without one of its most promising players, as Karl has been ruled out for the World Cup. The 18-year-old, who had 17 goal contributions for Bayern Munich this season, could miss up to two months</cite>.

items.headline: USA's Richards expected ready vs Paraguay
items.body: <cite index="21-23">Richards didn't face Germany in the United States' final World Cup tuneup, but the Crystal Palace defender recently said he'll be ready for Friday's opener against Paraguay</cite>. <cite index="20-8,20-9">The U.S. men's national team enters the tournament after a disappointing 2-1 loss to Germany in Chicago, a result that did little to ease concerns about Mauricio Pochettino's squad, with center back Chris Richards having yet to return from an ankle injury</cite>.

items.headline: Argentina's Messi targets opener despite hamstring
items.body: <cite index="22-15,22-16">Messi left his most recent Inter Miami appearance early with a hamstring issue, though it was seemingly a precautionary move. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner didn't play in Argentina's latest pre-World Cup friendly but is likely to be available for its opener against Algeria</cite>.

items.headline: Brazil's Estêvão ruled out with hamstring
items.body: <cite index="19-8,19-9">Estêvão pulled up against Manchester United in April with a hamstring injury that left him in tears. The initial prognosis was positive, suggesting a two-week absence, but it soon became clear things were much more serious, and he has been left off Brazil's preliminary squad</cite>.

items.headline: Africa sends record 10 teams
items.body: <cite index="7-20,7-21">Africa sends ten teams to the 2026 World Cup, its largest ever representation. Morocco leads the group after its historic 2022 semi final run</cite>. <cite index="9-27">The African qualifiers include Algeria, Cape Verde, Egypt, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Morocco, Senegal, South Africa, Tunisia</cite>.

items.headline: Europe sends 16 teams to tournament
items.body: <cite index="7-28,7-29">Europe sends 16 teams to the 2026 World Cup. France, Spain, England, Portugal and Germany enter as major contenders, while Bosnia and Herzegovina returns after its 2014 debut</cite>.

items.headline: South America maintains six-team presence
items.body: <cite index="7-24,7-25">South America sends six teams to the 2026 World Cup. Argentina arrives as defending champion, while Brazil keeps its record of appearing at every men's World Cup</cite>.

items.headline: New pathway prevents top teams early meetings
items.body: <cite index="1-23,1-24,1-25">In the pursuit of competitive balance, two pathways have been created to the semifinals that will prevent the two highest-ranking teams from meeting before the final should they win their respective groups. Spain is the highest-ranked team in the tournament, with defending champion Argentina ranked second. Those two nations were drawn into opposite pathways</cite>.

metadata.purpose: Prevent top seeds meeting before final

items.headline: Round of 32 adds elimination stage depth
items.body: <cite index="2-3">The knockout stage will be played in a single-elimination format, starting with the round of 32 on June 28 and culminating with the final on July 19</cite>. <cite index="1-20">The eight best third-place teams will advance to the Round of 32</cite>.
